title: Cyclone feed pump, gland seal failure
tests: Sound, well-evidenced analysis (should NOT be over-flagged); forced deterioration; clear-cut.
summary: Gland packing on the duty cyclone feed pump P-2301 failed for the fourth time in 10 months. Slurry was pushed into the gland because gland water pressure was below stuffing box pressure. The shared gland water strainer was 80% blocked; rounds only ask 'gland water OK?'. The tree is mostly sound and evidenced. The test is that the AI does not invent problems.

problem.title: Repeat gland failures on cyclone feed pump P-2301
problem.site: Gold processing plant, grinding circuit, Kalgoorlie WA
problem.whatHappened: P-2301 was stopped at about 02:40 on 18 Mar 2026 after the packing gland ran hot and leaked slurry across the pump base. Gland packing and shaft sleeve were found scored. This is the fourth gland failure on P-2301 in 10 months. Standby P-2302 was started and the circuit ran at reduced throughput for about 6 hours.
problem.where: Packing gland and shaft sleeve, drive side of P-2301 stuffing box.
problem.when: Normal duty, no recent process upset. Events spread across shifts; this one was found on the 2-hourly round.
problem.impact: Grinding throughput cut by about 35% for 6 hours. About 2 m3 of slurry spilled and cleaned up. Gland repack and sleeve replacement. No injury.
problem.duty: Primary mill discharge to cyclone cluster, duty/standby

evidence.title: Gland water pressure readings, P-2301 and P-2302
evidence.note: 18 Mar: gland water 0.4 bar at the P-2301 stuffing box. Stuffing box slurry pressure about 1.9 bar from the discharge gauge, so slurry was being pushed into the gland. P-2302 gland water 0.6 bar.

evidence.title: Failed gland packing and shaft sleeve
evidence.note: Packing rings hard and glazed with fine grit through the layers. Sleeve scored about 0.8 mm deep under the packing.

evidence.title: Gland water header strainer
evidence.note: Common header strainer found about 80% blocked with scale and rubber flakes. No record of when it was last cleaned.

evidence.title: Operator round sheet
evidence.note: Round sheet asks only 'Gland water OK?' with a tick box. No pressure or flow value recorded. All ticked for the last 3 months.

evidence.title: Work order history P-2301
evidence.note: Four gland repack or sleeve WOs in 10 months, each closed 'repacked gland, ok'. No WO or PM task for the gland water strainer.

evidence.title: Operator and fitter conversation
evidence.note: Operators judge flow by eye on the rotameter; the glass is stained and hard to read. Fitters set the gland followers by feel.

evidence.title: P&ID and DCS alarm list
evidence.note: No pressure or flow instrument on the gland water header. No alarm or interlock to the pumps.

tree.text: Gland on cyclone feed pump P-2301 failed, fourth time in 10 months

children.text: Packing glazed and sleeve scored by abrasive slurry entering the gland
Gland water pressure was below stuffing box slurry pressure, so slurry was pushed into the packing
Common gland water header strainer was about 80% blocked, restricting flow to both pumps
Strainer was not cleaned and low flow was not noticed on rounds; the rotameter is hard to read
No strainer cleaning task in the PM plan, and the round sheet has no pressure or flow limit
Gland water supply has no low-pressure or low-flow alarm or interlock
Gland followers are adjusted by feel, with no set leakage standard
No standard job plan for gland packing and adjustment

task.description: Remove and clean gland water header strainer, record gland water pressure before and after

actions.description: Fit gland water low-pressure alarm on the header, wired to the DCS

spares.coverage: Packing and a spare sleeve were in stock.

problemDraft.roughNotes: p2301 gland blew out again 0240 nights. packing hard n glazed, sleeve scored. gland water looked ok on rotameter when i checked but pressure gauge on the stuffing box was low. 4th time since last may. swapped to p2302, tonnes down for about 6 hrs. spill round the base ~2 cubes, cleaned up by day shift. no one hurt.

mustSuggest.idea: Strainer cleaning is not owned or scheduled, so low flow went unnoticed
No PM task or flow/pressure instrument on the gland water header
Source of the scale and rubber flakes in the water supply (water quality, hose or lining breaking down)

acceptable: Single shared header feeds both pumps, so one blockage hits duty and standby
Gland water pressure setpoint never defined
wrongOrDangerous: Replace the pump or change the packing grade as the answer
Tighten the gland harder (burns the sleeve)

mustNotFlag: stopped_at_physical on n3 (human and system causes sit beneath it)
blame on n4 (it is written as a system gap)
no_preventive (n5 and n6 both have actions)
no_task_interval on a2 (4 weeks and a craft are set)
deterioration_undecided (a wear cause is not left undecided: n1, n2 are physical states, forced is clear from the tree text)
challenge.expectation: At most 2 issues, all low or medium. Summary says the analysis looks sound. Acceptable low-level points: n7/n8 hypothesis with no evidence; a3 not yet done; no horizontal expansion to other pumps on the shared header.
deliberateWeaknesses: None deliberate. The tree is sound. Two low-level gaps are left on purpose: the gland adjustment branch (n7, n8) is still a hypothesis with no evidence.

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Slurry entered the gland because gland water pressure fell below slurry pressure. We caused it by not maintaining or monitoring the supply.
corrective: Repack and replace sleeve (already done, a1): the AI should not repeat it

preventive.what: Clean gland water strainer on both pumps and record gland water pressure
preventive.interval: 4 weeks (or on a hours run basis)

preventive.what: Gland water pressure and flow reading against a stated minimum above stuffing box pressure, on rounds
Change the round sheet from 'OK?' tick to a recorded pressure with a limit

preventive.craft: Instrument technician (a3 already covers the alarm: do not duplicate)

capa.spares: Hold packing set, 1 sleeve and 1 strainer basket for the 10/8 pump; sleeve and packing already in stock so say min holding, not a new purchase.
capa.rollout: Other pumps on the same gland water header and any slurry pump using packing with a shared supply.
unacceptable: Shorten the gland repack interval as the countermeasure
Retrain operators as the only action
